name: Natalie Clifford Barney
bio: American heiress, poet, and Paris salon hostess who, per McDermott, 'saw herself as a latter day Sappho', and whose Quelques Portraits-Sonnets de Femmes (1900) made her notorious for openly lesbian verse. She opened a correspondence with Olive Custance after Opals (1897), wooed her with love poems, hosted her in Paris, and travelled with her in Italy around 1901; her memoir Souvenirs Indiscrets (1960) recounts the episode, including a plan to gather Custance and Renée Vivien into a Sapphic community at Mytilene. Her later, celebrated Left-Bank circle (Vivien, Romaine Brooks, and others) lies outside this web's scope.
bio_note: Dates (1876-1972) and the wooing account from Sarah Parker's Y90s Custance biography (read in full 2026-08-03); pursuit/Italy details from McDermott's Fortnightly Review profile (2020); 'rumoured entanglements' framing from Parker 2011 (AM p. 1), citing Wickes 1977 and Souhami 2004.
